headline: Building AI Agent Harnesses: Two Architectural Approaches
summary: This InfoQ article breaks down the concept of an 'agent harness' — the orchestration layer that wraps an LLM to give it tools, memory, and control flow — and walks through two concrete ways engineers can build one, from lightweight custom loops to more structured frameworks.
why_it_matters: As you move toward AI Application Engineering with LLM apps on ServiceNow, understanding harness design patterns directly informs how you architect agentic workflows, tool-calling, and control loops in production systems.

headline: QCon AI New York 2026 Previews Sessions on Agent Authorization and Production Evaluation
summary: QCon AI New York 2026 has released its session lineup, covering topics from agent authorization models to methods for evaluating AI systems once they're in production.
why_it_matters: These sessions cover the practical, operational side of shipping LLM-based agents — authorization and evaluation — both core concerns for building robust enterprise AI applications like the ones you work on.

headline: Appeals Court Upholds Pentagon's 'Supply Chain Risk' Designation for Anthropic
summary: A U.S. appeals court has upheld the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk, a ruling with implications for how AI vendors are vetted for government and defense-related contracts.
why_it_matters: This case highlights growing regulatory scrutiny of AI vendors and supply chains, a trend worth tracking as it may shape which LLM providers are viable for enterprise/government deployments similar to ServiceNow environments.

headline: Stateless MCP Design Eliminates Session Affinity for AWS Deployments
summary: A new stateless approach to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) removes the need for session affinity when deploying MCP servers on AWS, simplifying scaling and load balancing for tool-serving infrastructure.
why_it_matters: MCP is becoming a standard way to connect LLMs to external tools and data; a stateless design pattern is directly relevant to building scalable, production-grade LLM applications.

headline: Podcast Explores Enterprise AI Adoption vs. Open-Source Sovereignty
summary: This InfoQ podcast discusses the tension between enterprises adopting proprietary AI platforms and the push toward open-source, sovereign AI stacks that reduce vendor lock-in.
why_it_matters: Understanding the trade-offs between enterprise and open-source AI stacks is useful context as you develop LLM applications within an enterprise platform like ServiceNow.
